setup.title: Set up the environment
setup.description: Install Python and the model's dependencies. Only needed once per machine, but everything downstream depends on it.

vehicle-tracking.name: Vehicle tracking data cleaning and analysis

end_time.label: End time
end_time.description: When it ends. The two together are the window the run covers.

simulation_step_sec.label: Simulation step
simulation_step_sec.description: The clock tick. Waits and travel times are rounded up to a whole number of these.

simulation_mode.label: Simulation mode
simulation_mode.description: Which of the model's modes the run uses, and so how trips are generated.

speed_based_routing.label: Speed-based routing
speed_based_routing.description: Route on travel time rather than on distance.

agents.label: Agents introduced per period
agents.description: How many agents join the road in each period, so demand rises and falls across the day.

animation_agents.label: Animation agents
animation_agents.description: How many agents' trips are written out for the animation to play back.

probability_hail.label: Probability of hailing
probability_hail.description: The chance an agent takes a fare off the road rather than waiting at a taxi rank.

max_total_distance_m.label: Max total distance
max_total_distance_m.description: How far an agent can travel on a charge before it has to swap.

buffer_distance.label: Buffer distance
buffer_distance.description: Range held back in reserve, so a vehicle swaps before it strands. It also bounds how far from a station an agent can start.

passenger_max_dist.label: Passenger max distance
passenger_max_dist.description: The furthest a fare-carrying trip can be.

deviation_factor.label: Deviation factor
deviation_factor.description: The assumed ratio of road distance to straight-line distance, used to size the search for a destination.

swap_wait_sec.label: Swap wait
swap_wait_sec.description: How long a battery swap takes.

pickup_wait_sec.label: Pickup wait
pickup_wait_sec.description: How long an agent waits at a pickup before the passenger trip starts.

roads.title: Extract the road network
roads.description: Pull the road graph for the region out of OpenStreetMap. This becomes the network every agent routes over.

area.title: Define the area
area.description: Draw or import the boundary the simulation covers. Trips are generated and routed inside it, with a buffer for journeys that stray outside.

stations.title: Place swap stations
stations.description: Choose where battery swap stations go, either by hand or by running the facility location optimisation over expected demand.

configure.title: Set scenario parameters
configure.description: Set the simulation window, agent numbers, distances and routing options in the scenario file. This is what the Parameters page shows.

simulate.title: Run the simulation
simulate.description: Step the agents through the day: fares, pickups, passenger journeys and battery swaps, all routed over the road network.

animate.title: Watch the trips
animate.description: Play the whole fleet's day back over the map, with each agent coloured by what it is doing at that moment.

stationView.title: Watch the swap stations
stationView.description: Step through each station's posts and queue to see where vehicles waited and for how long.

analyse.title: Read the analysis
analyse.description: Charts and tables summarising distances, waits, queues and station use across the run.

hail_rank.summary: Agents find passengers by travelling towards a nearby taxi rank, with a defined probability of being hailed en route versus after waiting at the taxi rank.  Passenger destinations within the scenarion area and within a defined maximum distance are randomly selected.

define.title: Place taxi ranks
define.description: Import the ranks where agents wait for fares. Agents pick between hailing on the road and queueing at a rank.

demand_model.summary: Demand points are specified within defined categories. Trip frequencies are defined between pairs of categories. Trips are then generated with these frequencies, each trip a random selection from the source and estination demand point categories.  The closest idle agent is assigned to each trip.

define.title: Place demand points
define.description: Mark where trips start and end. The demand point editor puts them on the map and gives each one a weight.

define.title: Set demand frequencies
define.description: Say how often trips are generated at each point through the day, so demand rises and falls with the peaks.

distribution.summary: Agents work a fare-wait / pickup / passenger cycle, with trip distances and fare waits drawn from from pre-defined distributions.

define.title: Define trip distributions
define.description: Derive the distance and waiting-time distributions from tracked trips. The simulation draws from these rather than from fixed demand points.

analyse.title: Compare against the target distributions
analyse.description: Plot what the run actually produced against the distributions it was asked for - trip distance and fare wait, as both per-bin share and cumulative percentage. The simulation does not sample the target directly: it draws a distance band and then looks for a road node that far away, which can fail, and it refuses destinations that would leave a vehicle unable to reach a swap station. Every one of those is a place the realised distribution can drift from the target.

calibration.summary: Agent trips are generated by applying routing to actual journeys with known start and end locations and times. These trips provide the basis of calibrating the road speeds that are applied to all model types.  In addition, trip distance and wait time distributions are derived and applied to scenarios with a 'trip distribution' model type.

define.title: Import tracked trips
define.description: Load the recorded vehicle journeys, clean the GPS noise out of them, and map-match them onto the road network.

run.title: Chain segments into journeys
run.description: Decide which consecutive segments are really one journey. For each pair the router is asked for the direct path from the first trip's start to the second's end and compares it with what the vehicle actually covered: a near-identical time means stopping there cost nothing and the two are one journey, while a detour means there was a real destination between them. The verdicts are then applied to produce a chained trip file, following runs of chained pairs so A-B-C collapses to one journey.

run.title: Generate trip routes
run.description: Snap each recorded trip's endpoints to the road network and route between them with the same weights the simulation uses, writing one file per vehicle in the format a simulation run produces. The timeline stays the recorded one: the routed hop times are rescaled to the duration actually observed, and the gaps between trips become idle points.

analyse.title: Check the fit
analyse.description: Distance discrepancy and segment chaining charts show how closely the routed trips track what the GPS logger actually recorded.

analyse.title: Analyse idle gaps and trip length
analyse.description: Split trips by how long the vehicle had been stationary beforehand - under a minute, up to ten, up to an hour, longer - and plot the trip distances in each band. A bin search finds which gap bands show the strongest association between consecutive idle gaps, and a correlation check asks whether the gap before a trip is related to the gap before the one prior to it.

analyse.title: Calibrate road speeds
analyse.description: Compare simulated journey times against the tracked ones and adjust the per-highway-type speeds until the two agree. The result becomes the global road speed table.

analyse.title: Calibrate trip distance and wait distributions
analyse.description: Fit the distance and fare-wait distributions to the tracked trips, so a run can draw journeys from measured behaviour rather than from fixed demand points. These are what a trip distribution scenario then uses.

analyse.title: Measure the deviation factor
analyse.description: Measure the ratio of road distance driven to straight-line distance between start and end. It is a property of the road network rather than of the fleet, so it has to be measured per city; trip distribution runs use it to turn a drawn road distance into the straight-line radius they search for a destination in.
